analysis:
This PR touches only CI threat-review tooling. None of it is provider, coordinator or native-runtime code, so no asset, boundary or threat in the provider threat model is affected (A-001..A-017, TB-002/003/007/009/010/011, T-041, T-053 and others).

budget_scan.py:
- Adds a `finished` flag (head 85, 112, 400).
- Adds plan_calls (head 317-327), which calls the optional `self.paid.plan_calls(count)` before the source, integration and depth stages (head 304, 332, 367).
- Validation, citation checks, the repair logic and cache-identity derivation are unchanged.
- plan_calls resets `paid.last_request` to {} without the hasattr guard used elsewhere. This is harmless: it is only reached when the planner exists.

diagnostics.py (head 82-83):
- Exports `finished` plus the bedrock_call_policy/limit/ceiling/planned_calls keys from the snapshot to the content-free diagnostics artifact.
- These are presumably numeric or policy metrics from `paid.metrics()`. Their producer is not in this batch, so integration should confirm they carry no secrets or free text.

threat-model-review.yml:
- Removes the workflow_dispatch pr_number path and its manually resolved event. This reduces surface: there is no longer an arbitrary-PR dispatch, and Bedrock is no longer enabled for dispatch.
- preflight now defaults to true, and the review job runs only on pull_request_target.
- timeout-minutes changes from 20 to 60, and THREAT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is set to 3000.
- The configurable BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_CALLS (default 12) is replaced by a fixed workload policy with BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_WORKLOAD_CALLS=100 (head 135-136).

Cost-amplification question for integration:
- A same-repo PR, or a fork PR when BEDROCK_SCAN_ALLOW_FORKS is set, could drive up to 100 paid calls per run, and runs retrigger on synchronize.
- Whether this is bounded depends on the unseen Bedrock adapter's plan_calls enforcement and any dollar ledger.
- This is CI billing, outside the provider threat model's scope, and enforcement source is not supplied. It is recorded as an unverified contract rather than a finding.

No regression to threat-model controls was identified.
